title: prefill-decode: chunked prefill + speculative prefill + stage overlap scheduling optimizations
author: Maya Kapoor
release_notes: Performance: Reduced end-to-end prefill+decode latency and improved throughput by overlapping prefill and decode stages, adding chunked and speculative prefill paths. Includes scheduler heuristics and new telemetry for stage overlap.
description: Motivation: Prefill (context encoding/KV cache population) and decode (token generation) are a dominant portion of end-to-end serving latency for long-context and interactive workloads. We observed underutilized GPU work during multi-request workloads where prefill work stalls waiting for full sequences, and decode stalls waiting for KV availability. This PR implements three coordinated optimizations: 1) chunked prefill - break long prefill sequences into fixed-size chunks so KV cache and kernels can start being consumed earlier; 2) speculative prefill - issue best-effort prefill chunks for anticipated next segments (warm KV/cache) when request patterns indicate high locality; 3) stage overlap scheduling - scheduler changes to allow decode work to run concurrently with later prefill chunks when safe (compatible KV state) and to prioritise small decode-critical shards to reduce tail latency. Approach: - runtime: add PrefillChunker and SpeculativePrefillPath; prefill_manager now emits chunked tasks and speculative hints to scheduler. - scheduler: new OverlapAwareScheduler that tracks KV consistency windows and allows eager decode execution when overlap constraints are met; added queue priorities for decode-critical shards. - kv_cache: thread-safety hardening for concurrent chunked writes and eviction interactions; lightweight sequence-level write guards instead of global locks. - kernels: minor kernel selection tweaks to prefer low-latency attention kernels for decode-critical shards and maintain throughput kernels for bulk prefill chunks. Benchmarks (perf-lab synthetic + internal canary): - baseline: standard prefill->decode pipeline (no overlap) - canary results: 15-22% increase in tokens/sec for mixed long-context interactive workload; 18% reduction in p99 latency; median latency improved by ~12%; unit cost per 1M tokens reduced ~10% due to better packing and earlier KV reuse. Implementation notes: - chunk size is configurable by runtime flags (default 128 tokens) and adaptive heuristic added (prefers chunking when context > 1024 tokens). - speculative prefill is opt-in per deployment and gated by runtime flag; only enabled for clients with high locality signals (per-route telemetry). - OverlapAwareScheduler includes conservative safety checks to ensure speculative/overlapped decode never observes stale KV. Testing: - microbench unit tests for PrefillChunker and KV write guards. - end-to-end perf tests added under tests/bench/prefill_perf_test.py capturing latency percentiles and throughput. - fuzzing harness for race conditions in kv_cache. - canary rollout: staged on Dedicated pool with 5% traffic, monitoring rollback if regen-quality or latency regressions detected. Checklist: - [x] unit tests & integration tests added - [x] perf harness and benchmarks included - [x] telemetry/metrics for overlap utilization and speculative hits - [x] docs: short design note and runtime flags - [x] rollout plan documented Known limitations: - Speculative prefill can slightly increase work for low-locality workloads; default is off for hosted until heuristics stabilize. - Chunking adds a small scheduling overhead; benefits are most apparent for long-context workloads. Related: ENG-2129 (prefill scheduling), ENG-2175 (kv concurrency), SUP-834 (customer incident: prefill stalls under long context).
commits_summary: 5 commits: initial chunked prefill prototype; add speculative prefill path and feature flag; OverlapAwareScheduler implementation; kv_cache concurrency fixes + tests; docs and perf benchmarks.
review_comments: Rafael Ortiz (reviewer): Overall looks good. Two concerns: 1) please justify the choice of default chunk size 128 and add unit tests to cover edge-cases (very small/borderline lengths). 2) KV write path changes need a small perf microbenchmark to ensure we didn't regress single-request latency.

Maya Kapoor (author): Added adaptive chunking heuristic and unit tests for edges (small context <chunk size). Added a microbenchmark in tests/bench to capture single-request latency; results included in PR description.
Sofia Nadeem (reviewer): Can we add telemetry for speculative prefill hit/miss and a circuit-breaker to disable speculative path if miss-rate > X?

Maya Kapoor (author): Added metrics: prefill.speculative.hits, prefill.speculative.misses and a runtime flag speculative.prefill.circuit_breaker.threshold (default 0.5). Circuit-breaker implemented in PrefillChunker.

Jordan Li (reviewer): kv_cache concurrency looks correct but suggest replacing one global mutex with sequence-level guards to reduce contention (see inline comment in kv_cache.cpp). Also please ensure no additional ephemeral allocations are introduced in the hot path.

Maya Kapoor (author): Switched to sequence-level write guards per suggestion and removed an unnecessary temporary buffer in the hot write path; reran perf bench — no single-request regressions observed.

perf-bench — pass (canary vs baseline: 18% p99 latency reduction, 15-22% throughput uplift depending on load profile)
